theme: Unit 22 review, In Christ, Prison & Pastoral Epistles
memoryText: He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation. For by him all things were created, in heaven and on earth.
memoryVerseMeditation:
Paul lifts our eyes to Christ. He is “the image of the invisible God.” No one has seen God, but we see him in Jesus. He is “the firstborn of all creation,” which means he has the rank and inheritance of the firstborn, not that he was created. “For by him all things were created, in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones or dominions or rulers or authorities.” The powers that the Colossians feared are creatures, made by him and for him.

This verse is the foundation of the whole Prison and Pastoral section. If Christ is this great, we are secure in him, the church is his body, our work is for him, and our hope is his appearing. Say it slowly. Each phrase is a reason to worship.
unitRecap: This unit took us through the Prison and Pastoral Epistles. Ephesians showed us God’s plan from eternity: chosen in Christ, saved by grace through faith, made one new people, and equipped to walk in love, light, and the whole armor of God. Psalms 68 and 110 celebrated the ascended Christ as priest-king. Philippians showed joy in chains, the humility and exaltation of Christ in the great hymn, and the surpassing worth of knowing him. Colossians declared the supremacy of Christ over all things and taught us to live in him, setting our minds on things above and doing everything in the name of the Lord Jesus. We paused to consider election, the church, the person of Christ as fully God and fully man, and ordinary work as a calling. In 1 and 2 Thessalonians, we learned to wait for the Lord’s return with hope and with work, and to stand firm in persecution. Psalms 27, 138, and 139 taught us to seek the LORD’s face, give thanks with the whole heart, and be searched and led by the one who made us. In 1 Timothy we learned how the household of God should live, with sound doctrine, prayer, and godly leaders. In 2 Timothy we heard Paul’s last words: guard the gospel, rightly handle the word, and trust that all Scripture is breathed out by God. Titus showed how grace trains us for good works, and Philemon showed the gospel at work in one friendship, with Paul standing in for the guilty.

reviewQuestions.question: Ephesians 2:8-10 and Titus 3:4-7 both say we are saved by grace, not works, and yet for good works. How do these fit together?
reviewQuestions.prompt: Write in your own words how salvation by grace leads to a life of good works, and give an example from your own life.

reviewQuestions.question: Philippians 2:5-11 and Colossians 1:15-20 both describe Christ. What do they teach about who he is and what he has done?
reviewQuestions.prompt: List three truths about Christ from these passages and say how each strengthens your trust or worship.

reviewQuestions.question: Paul writes many of these letters from prison. What do Philippians and 2 Timothy show about how a believer can face hardship?
reviewQuestions.prompt: Choose a hardship you or someone you know is facing and apply one truth from these letters.

reviewQuestions.question: 2 Timothy 3:16-17 says all Scripture is breathed out by God. What difference does this make to how you read the Bible?
reviewQuestions.prompt: Describe one change you will make to your reading habits, based on what Scripture is and what it does.

prayerPrompts: Thank God for the letters of Paul and what they have taught you.
Thank him for Christ in whom all things hold together.
Ask him to keep the unit verse before you.
